classification_rationale: code-behavior gap: a missing bound check, not a prose issue
summary: No bound check: a too-high reserved-connections value locks out every ordinary client, not just under load.

classification_rationale: clarifying comment, no behavior claim contradicted
trigger: reading scenario N's password-absence log grep as a complete secrecy proof
summary: A clean server-log grep for a password's absence doesn't prove the password never appears in this process's own argv.

classification_rationale: a required migration-step doc (item 2, changed operator workflow) named no command
trigger: operator follows the Patroni existing-cluster migration instructions verbatim
summary: Patroni migration step said 'set it in the DCS parameters' with no literal command, unlike the single-node path's exact ALTER SYSTEM.

classification_rationale: a comment's own currency claim was inaccurate
trigger: a future edit lowers max_connections in the Patroni YAML template without updating the bound check's literal
summary: The bound-check literal (200-3) and the rendered max_connections value were two independent hand-written literals 86 lines apart, not truly 'read from the same place' as the comment claimed.

classification_rationale: required doc item 2 (upgrade step) under-weighted a new failure mode
trigger: operator skims only the upgrading.md bullet list
summary: The breaking-changes bullet list didn't separately call out that a misconfigured reserved-connections value now blocks the Postgres CONTAINER (not just the server binary) from starting.

classification_rationale: not a required-doc category; an observability capability gap
trigger: operator misconfigures max_connections sizing, or organic fleet growth drifts the formula's assumptions
summary: The connection-budget sizing formula is a paper calculation with no runtime feedback loop (no gauge/metric shows actual headroom before it's exhausted).

classification_rationale: test-coverage gap, not a required-doc category
trigger: the shipped yuzu-postgres/yuzu-postgres-ha images' init scripts change without a corresponding automated boundary test
summary: Scenario N boots the stock postgres:18.4-bookworm image, never the actual yuzu-postgres/yuzu-postgres-ha images, so the new init-script GRANT/ALTER SYSTEM/bound-check code paths have zero automated coverage of their own.

classification_rationale: required migration-step doc omitted an apply step
trigger: operator on an existing Patroni cluster runs patronictl edit-config verbatim and stops
summary: patronictl edit-config only writes the DCS config and marks the member pending-restart; it does not itself apply a postmaster-context GUC. The documented step never said to also patronictl restart.

classification_rationale: no doc named the recovery path for this specific race
trigger: container killed between GRANT and ALTER SYSTEM during first boot only (single-node image)
summary: Postgres's initdb-runs-once convention means the whole init-script sequence never re-runs once the data directory exists; a kill in the narrow GRANT-then-ALTER-SYSTEM window leaves the grant present but the GUC still at Postgres's default (0), silently.

classification_rationale: no doc named this residual, and no runtime mechanism exists
trigger: operator runs patronictl edit-config to change max_connections on an already-bootstrapped, running cluster
summary: The boot-time bound check runs once, at cluster bootstrap. Nothing re-validates the reserved_connections/max_connections relationship on an already-running cluster after a live GUC edit.

classification_rationale: no runbook text distinguished the two causes
trigger: either a max_connections exhaustion (#4943) or a genuine Postgres overload (#4944) occurs in production
summary: Both failure causes collapse to the identical /readyz pg_reachable=unreachable verdict and the identical alert; only the server log's exact refusal text distinguishes them, and no runbook said so.

classification_rationale: no doc named the recovery/re-verification step after this class of event
trigger: the app role is dropped/recreated (credential rotation, DR restore) without re-running GRANT pg_use_reserved_connections
summary: Both init scripts are first-boot-only and never re-applied; a role recreation event silently defeats the #4943 mechanism with no automated detection.

classification_rationale: a genuinely new behavior (the shipped default) not called out for the fresh-install case
trigger: a fresh install or reinstall (new empty data volume), not an in-place upgrade of an existing database
summary: A fresh volume silently picks up the new default-40 reservation, reducing available connections for third-party tooling by up to 40 versus a pre-release deployment; only the in-place-upgrade case was explicitly covered.

classification_rationale: a comment contradicting the actual code value
trigger: reading the scenario-L header description against its implementation
summary: Header said `docker update --cpus 0.05`; the actual, empirically-retuned value is 0.01 -- the header was never updated when the parameter was recalibrated.

classification_rationale: running --help produced truncated, contradictory output vs. its own convention
trigger: any operator running --help after scenario N was added
summary: The --help sed range was extended past the old convention's stopping point, landing mid-sentence inside a trailer paragraph.

classification_rationale: a fast-follow named in prose with no tracked owner/timeline
trigger: the 'fast-follow' language in server-admin.md has no corresponding tracked issue
summary: A documented compensating control (manual re-verification) for a SOC2-relevant availability guarantee should have a tracked remediation issue, not just prose naming a fast-follow. Both fast-follows now tracked: #5015 (live GUC revalidation) and #5016 (grant-loss self-check).

classification_rationale: the documented recovery instruction didn't work for this specific image/ordering
trigger: the single-node image's boot-time bound check refuses AFTER role/database/grant already exist on the initialized data directory
summary: 'Lower the env var and redeploy' does not actually retrigger anything on the single-node image, because Postgres's initdb-once convention means the init script never re-runs once the data directory exists -- the naive recovery path silently never applies the fix.

trigger: a customer's ops team skims the upgrade notes rather than reading closely
summary: Fresh-install / in-place-upgrade / manual-apply were all present but unevenly weighted in one dense paragraph, risking a skimming reader missing the in-place-upgrade case.

classification_rationale: changelog fragment scope narrower than the actual behavior change
trigger: a customer reads only the assembled CHANGELOG.md, not upgrading.md
summary: The changelog fragment described the reserve+grant+scenarios but never mentioned the new boot-time hard-refusal behavior, which only appeared in upgrading.md.
